target_customer: Plaintiff personal injury, mass tort and medical malpractice law firms that need medical records for cases
problem: Law firms wait weeks or months to get medical records from providers with varied back office rules; chasing requests is slow and manual.
business_model: Per request or service fee for end to end medical record retrieval, with software integrations into legal case management
product_category: AI enabled medical record retrieval for legal teams

founders.name: Alvaro Rivera
founders.background_notes: A profile site says he saw the problem while running a home health agency; that is a secondary directory and not verified.

founders.name: Austin Mills
founders.background_notes: Listed as co-founder and COO on YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Hard part is operational and data work, building a facility database and automating request submission across varied provider portals and fax processes, rather than research level ML.

defensibility.rationale: A proprietary facility requirements database and integrations with case management systems such as Filevine create some lock in; the operational layer is copyable by rivals.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; in July 2026 Filevine announced a partnership to embed Codes Health rather than build it.

market_need_then: Personal injury firms spend heavily on medical record requests and face long turnaround; the Filevine release says hundreds of firms use the product, which is a partner statement and not independently verified.

branding.domain_note: Uses codeshealth.com (not an exact .com of the plain name).

identity.visual_style: Brown textured kraft paper look with envelope and stacked document imagery
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, tagline 'get the records. build the case.'

branding.brand_signature: Kraft paper and envelope visual style with the tagline get the records. build the case.

brand_strength.rationale: Coherent visual identity on the site and a partner press release, but no press about the brand, and the name 'Codes' is generic and suggests medical coding rather than records retrieval.

outcome_analysis: Codes Health is an active New York company with about 45 staff that sells medical record retrieval to plaintiff law firms, and in July 2026 it gained distribution through a Filevine partnership. Funding amounts are not verified, so the stage and scale of its financing remain unclear, though named investors include Y Combinator, Haystack and Amplify Partners.
notes: Funding unverified: Seedtable and CB Insights list 500K USD in 2024-09 with Y Combinator, Haystack Fund, Pathlight, Night Capital, General Catalyst; Simplify lists 130K total; one source says 13.5M. The Filevine release (2026-07-13) names Amplify Partners, Haystack and Y Combinator as backers without amounts or stage. No round recorded. Founder education is not given by the sources except that the Filevine release says the company was founded by MIT and Yale graduates without naming them, so education is left empty. No dated competitor sources near mid 2024 were found; competitor list left empty.
